sam: Noticed a weird drop in prefix cache warmup hit-rate after last night's hybrid-attn kernel + v2q quant rollout. Dash shows ~82% -> ~58% for high-cardinality prompt routes in us-west-2. Anyone else seeing this? :thinking:

maria: Yup, saw the same on a few production routes (conversations/*). Heatmap shows fewer early hits, warmup looks delayed. Link: https://grafana.company/r/xyz (shortlink) :chart_with_downwards_trend:

sam: Quick numbers from a sampled workload: baseline (pre-rollout) warmup_hit = 0.84, post-rollout = 0.61. Token-level latency stable but cost up because more generator steps hitting cold path.

aj: Did we change the cache key format or introduce any salting in the kernel build? Could be canonicalization drift if memory layout changed.

cheng: I don't think we changed app-side keying. The hybrid-attn kernel changed KV packing order (seq major -> block-major for fp4 pathway). That can surface if runtime used raw tensor bytes for fingerprinting.

sam: Good call. Quick grep in runtime shows one place still using raw tensor buffer fingerprint: `hash(buf.data(), buf.size())`. If packing changed, identical logical keys get different raw buffers.

maria: Oof. That would explain rekeying across compile variants. Can we confirm with a small repro?

cheng: Reproducer run I just kicked off (local with dev model v2q):
```
python tools/repro_caching.py --model open_v2q --prompt-file tests/prefixsamp.txt --profile
# output snippet
prefix_hits: 620/1000 (0.62)  <-- post-rollout
baseline_hits: 860/1000 (0.86) <-- pre-rollout
changed_keys_sample: 142
```

aj: So ~142 prompts got different keys. That matches the hit-rate delta. We should avoid raw-buffer fingerprints.

infra-bot: deploy-bot:rolled_out hybrid-attn/v2q -> us-west-2 at 2026-03-18T04:12Z.

deploy-bot: Canary passed health checks but warmup metrics not part of canary gate.

sam: Two immediate options: 1) roll back kernel in prod canary regions, 2) normalize keying to a logical fingerprint that is invariant to buffer packing and include compile id in key for safety. Rollback is easiest short-term.

taylor: Rolling back is disruptive for throughput gains we wanted. Suggest fast patch: change keying to canonicalize KV layout before hashing and add compile_id versioning to avoid silent mismatches across variants. That gives us correctness without sacrificing kernel perf.

cheng: Proposed patch (runtime/src/cache_key.cc):
```
// compute canonical prompt fingerprint
auto canonical = normalize_kv_layout(kv_tensor);
cache_key = fmt::format("{}:{}:{}", model_name, compile_id, sha1(canonical));
```
This normalizes ordering and pins keys to compile id so warmups from previous compile won't collide.

aj: I'll bench patch locally then push a short-lived rollout flag: `feature.runtime.canonical_kv_key=true` so we can flip without full rollback.

maria: Also recommend running a dedicated warmup sweep after enabling to re-populate keys. We saw the biggest hit on long-tail routes, warmup sweep should target them.

sam: Agreed. Aj, can you schedule warmup job and PR the canonicalization flag? If we confirm fix restores to ~0.84 I'll roll that into next minor runtime release.

aj: Scheduling warmup now (job id: warmup-210998). Will run across us-west-2/primary routes and report by EOD. :white_check_mark:

cheng: I'll draft the patch and a quick unit test to ensure hash invariant across buffer layout variants.

maria: Thanks — also adding a short alert to the perf dashboard to catch warmup regressions in future canaries.

sam: Great. Tracking metric: `prefix_cache.warmup_hit_rate` on the canonical eval set. We'll reconvene after warmup job results. :thumbsup:
